what: McCormick sells flavour: herbs, spices and seasoning mixes under its own name, Old Bay, French's mustard, Frank's RedHot and Cholula, and it also supplies flavourings in bulk to food manufacturers and restaurants.
customers: Supermarket shoppers for the branded half, and food companies and restaurant chains for the industrial half.
money: the larger part and most of the profit
custom flavourings for food makers and restaurant chains
moat: A spice aisle it largely controls, where shoppers reach for the familiar red cap, plus flavour formulas written into customers' recipes that cannot be changed without changing the product.
risks: Revenue has grown slowly, from $6.3B to $6.8B in four years
Own-label spices compete directly on price in a category where quality differences are hard to see
opportunities: 8.3 times earnings, unusually cheap for a branded food company with a 11.5% net margin
$926M of free cash flow and a dividend raised for about four decades
Analysts see about 18% upside, with 14 covering the stock
watch: Consumer segment volume growth, which shows whether the brands are holding share.
